_authoring.status: staged; not part of the production scenario loader
_authoring.scope: Western Kyushu: Ryuzoji 12 + Ito 8 + Sagara 6 = 26 distinct people.

sourceClasses.akaikeExcavation: municipal or prefectural excavation report citing edited local history
sourceClasses.indoExcavation: municipal or prefectural excavation report citing edited local history

_authoring.sourceBoundaries: Identity sources do not independently prove an exact lifespan or continuous 1560 service. Authored dates are explicit estimates. Source-qualified dates retain chronology or interpretation uncertainty.
_authoring.placementBoundaries: Castle stations aggregate regional households for scenario play, not claims of exact 1560 residence. Attributes, ranks and empty trait/tactic selections are manually authored design values. Deferred debut is conservative availability, not a proven genpuku date.
_authoring.kinBoundary: Only independently attested cousin, sibling or son relationships to the current leader receive isKin=true. A shared surname, marriage or membership in the household is insufficient.

excludedIdentities.name: 小河信安
excludedIdentities.reason: Saga municipal history printed 576–578 places his death in 1557. Secondary accounts place it in 1558; both precede 1560. The living baseline excludes him.
excludedIdentities.replacementBoundary: Supplemental Ogawa Nobutoshi is a distinct successor, not an alias or padded later death.

aliasBoundaries: Ogawa Nobuyasu/Takezumi is not Ogawa Nobutoshi/Nobutomo/Nobutsura.
Ito Yoshimasu (義益) is not Mancio/Sukemasu (祐益).
Ito Suketaka/祐兵 and his earlier name祐隆 are one identity.
Earlier Ochiai Wakasa-no-kami documents are not automatically assigned to Kaneasa.

off.ryuzoji-takanobu.support: Saga municipal history follows the lord and his 1584 death.
off.ryuzoji-takanobu.note: Leadership attributes are design values; no later conquests are assumed initially.

off.nabeshima-naoshige.support: Museum catalogue gives 1538–1618, service under Takanobu and a cousin relationship.
off.nabeshima-naoshige.note: Kin is independently sourced, not inferred from surname. Initial rank and station are design values.

off.nodomi-nobukage.support: Printed 564–565 names Nobukage among household administrators around 1548.
off.nodomi-nobukage.note: Lifespan is a design estimate fitting adult 1548 activity; no exact birth or death is proven.

off.ogawa-nobutoshi.support: Printed 578 distinguishes Kiyofusa's third son, renamed Nobutoshi, from the deceased Nobuyasu; printed 636 lists Nobutoshi in 1584.
off.ogawa-nobutoshi.note: Birth is a design estimate. This supplemental successor is not an alias or fabricated surviving Nobuyasu.

off.ryuzoji-naganobu.support: Saga municipal history printed 579 explicitly identifies Naganobu as Takanobu's younger brother.
off.ryuzoji-naganobu.note: Lifespan and Hasuike station are design estimates. Kin follows the explicit sibling relationship, not surname inference.

off.hyakutake-tomokane.support: Printed 642 records Tomokane's death in the 1584 battle.
off.hyakutake-tomokane.note: Birth, early service and abilities are design estimates; later battle narratives do not prove 1560 station.

off.ryuzoji-nobukane.support: Shiroishi gives 1532–1608 and identifies Takanobu's half-brother.
off.ryuzoji-nobukane.note: Hasuike station and rank are design values; later Suko residence is not backdated.

off.nabeshima-kiyofusa.support: Printed 564 names Kiyofusa as guardian; printed 578 identifies the father of Nobutoshi.
off.nabeshima-kiyofusa.note: Lifespan is an explicit design estimate. Marriage ties are not automatically a blood-kin declaration.

off.ryuzoji-masaie.support: Library exhibition gives 1556–1607; Shiroishi identifies Takanobu's eldest son.
off.ryuzoji-masaie.note: Design debut 1571 enforces the 15-year rule; he is not initially available or an early eligible heir.

off.narimatsu-nobukatsu.support: Printed 642 names Nobukatsu among the 1584 battle dead.
off.narimatsu-nobukatsu.note: Birth, initial service and station are design estimates; no later nickname creates an extra identity.

off.eriguchi-nobutsune.support: Printed 642 records Eriguchi Tohshichibei's 1584 death; this is the traditional Nobutsune identification.
off.eriguchi-nobutsune.note: Name mapping and birth remain source-qualified/design boundaries. Design debut 1563 prevents juvenile initial service.

off.enjoji-nobutane.support: Chiba municipal summit names Enjoji Nobutane; Saga printed 636 lists Enjoji Mino-no-kami in the 1584 army.
off.enjoji-nobutane.note: Birth and early station are design estimates. The title-to-person mapping is not a new duplicate officer.

off.ito-yoshisuke.note: Leadership attributes and initial castle placement are design values, not transplanted later borders.

off.ito-yoshimasu.support: Saito records death 1569 at age 24 and identifies his father Yoshisuke.
off.ito-yoshimasu.note: Birth 1546 follows the prescribed interpretation of age 24. Design debut 1561 prevents initial juvenile service.

off.ito-sukeyasu.support: Municipal booklet printed 7 names Sukeyasu among the 1572 generals and reports their deaths.
off.ito-sukeyasu.note: Birth, earlier service and Sadowara station are design estimates. No direct leader kin is inferred.

off.ochiai-kaneasa.support: Museum study identifies the signed name Kaneasa in 1569; earlier Wakasa-no-kami identities are disputed.
off.ochiai-kaneasa.note: Design lifespan/debut uses the explicit 1569 identification. Earlier same-title documents do not establish 1560 availability.

off.mera-shigekata.support: Municipal history names Shigekata, an Ito retainer, and his 1572 death.
off.mera-shigekata.note: Birth, earlier service and aggregated Sadowara station are design values, not proof of 1560 residence.

off.yamada-munemasa.support: Scholarly place dictionary cites Yamada Munemasa's memorandum concerning the 1577 Ito collapse.
off.yamada-munemasa.note: Lifespan and debut 1577 are conservative design choices. Munemasa/Masatoku is one identity, not two officers.

off.ito-suketaka.support: Scholarly dictionary gives 1559–1600 and identifies Yoshisuke's son.
off.ito-suketaka.note: Design debut 1574 enforces adulthood. Later Obi lordship does not imply 1560 service or an extra alias officer.

off.ito-mansho.support: University reference identifies Mancio/Sukemasu with birth 1569? and death 1612.
off.ito-mansho.note: Design debut 1584 keeps him unavailable initially. Future Ito affiliation models diplomatic talent, not proven secular vassal service.

off.sagara-yoshihi.support: Museum network gives 1544 birth and 1581 death; he inherited in 1555.
off.sagara-yoshihi.note: Design adulthood debut 1559 follows the core age rule despite historical childhood succession.

off.akaike-nagato.support: Excavation report printed 76 names Nagato as Okuchi lord under Yoshihi, citing Kuma Gaishi.
off.akaike-nagato.note: Lifespan and initial station are design estimates. Do not conflate Nagato with separately attested Nagazumi.

off.fukami-nagatomo.support: Keio catalogues Nagatomo's signed poetry sheet dated 1567-11-21.
off.fukami-nagatomo.note: Lifespan and debut 1567 are design choices; this dated identity alone does not prove 1560 service.

off.indo-yoriyasu.support: Prefectural excavation report printed 101 identifies Yoriyasu, father Shigeyasu and a later commemorative poem.
off.indo-yoriyasu.note: Lifespan and initial station are design estimates. No relationship to the current leader is invented.

off.marume-nagayoshi.support: Nishiki gives 1540–1629 and identifies the Sagara sword instructor.
off.marume-nagayoshi.note: Initial service and rank are design choices; no rare trait or locked tactic is assigned from later legends.

off.azuma-nagaaki.support: NDL/Keio catalogue identifies Azuma Danjo-no-chu Nagaaki on a 1545 Sagara elders' joint letter.
off.azuma-nagaaki.note: Lifespan and initial station are design estimates. No unknown family relationship is asserted.
